newsitem.title: UK: UK's most reviled murderess will die in prison.
newsitem.headline: UK's most reviled murderess will die in prison.

text.p: Myra Hindley, Britain's most reviled woman murderer, will spend the rest of her life in prison, her lawyers were told by the government on Tuesday.
Hindley, 54, was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1966 for the murders of five children, some of whose bodies were found buried on a lonely moor in northern England.
The "Moors Murders" carried out by Hindley and her lover Ian Brady shocked Britain to the core. The children were tortured and their agonies taped by the couple.
Home Secretary Michael Howard decreed in 1994 that Hindley should never be freed. Her lawyers claimed this was unlawful but Howard rejected their representations, according to government sources.
There are about 2,700 murderers serving life sentences in Britain, but few serve more than 25 years. The average time served by those released is around 14 years.

Hindley's lawyers, anticipating Tuesday's decision, said last week they would contest any "no-release" ruling in London's High Court. In December 1995, Hindley gave the first public account of her crimes, admitting she had been wicked and corrupt but claiming she was now a changed woman. "I was corrupt. I was wicked and evil and had behaved monstrously," she said. Hindley described herself as a political prisoner who was being used as a scapegoat by newspapers and politicians.

"The majority of people don't want to accept that people like myself can change, They prefer to keep me frozen in time together with that awful mugshot so that their attitudes, beliefs and perceptions can remain intact," she wrote.

A police mugshot of Hindley, peroxide blonde and staring, is one of the most recognised photographs in Britain. Hindley is in the same jail in northern England as Rosemary West, who was sentenced in November 1995 to life imprisonment for the murders of 10 young women and girls.
